sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Crunniuc, also called Cronnchu or Crunnchu, is an Irish hero. The goddess Macha, a fairy queen by some accounts, chose this mortal man and shared his farm. She brought riches and good fortune to both the man and his land. When Crunniuc said he meant to ride to the Assembly of Ulster, Macha, now with child, begged him to stay. He would hear none of it. So she won his word that he would name her to no one and never say she lived with him. Crunniuc broke that vow, boasting that Macha could outrun all the king's horses. A race followed that Macha won, only to fall at the line. The twins came even as she died, and she set on the whole region the curse known as the Debility of the Ulstermen. The records fall silent on Crunniuc after his wife's death, yet he can hardly have stayed well liked.

okr.objective: Crunniuc is the mortal husband whose boast led Macha to race, give birth to twins, and curse Ulster.
key_results: He was the mortal man chosen by the goddess or fairy queen Macha, who lived on his farm.
He broke his promise not to mention her and boasted she was faster than the king’s swiftest horses.
After Macha won the race, she gave birth to twins as she died and cursed the region with the Debility of the Ulstermen.
